problem.paragraph: Evaluate $$\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}$$ , where $$R$$ is the region bounded by the graphs of $$g_{1}(x) = x$$ and $$g_{2}(x) = x^{1 \slash 3}$$ in the first quadrant.

solution.paragraph: The region $$R$$ is shown in the accompanying figure. The points of intersection of the two curves are found by solving the equation $$x = x^{1 \slash 3}$$ , giving $$x = 0$$ and $$x = 1$$ . Using Equation (20), we find

$$\begin{array}{l} {{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= {\int_{0}^{1}{\left\lbrack {\int_{x}^{x^{1 \slash 3}}{\left( {x + y} \right)dy}} \right\rbrack dx}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= {\int_{0}^{1}{\left( \left. {xy + \frac{1}{2}y^{2}} \right|_{x}^{x^{1 \slash 3}} \right)dx}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= {\int_{0}^{1}{\left\lbrack {\left( {x^{4 \slash 3} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2 \slash 3}} \right) - \left( {x^{2} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}} \right)} \right\rbrack dx}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= {\int_{0}^{1}{\left( {x^{4 \slash 3} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2 \slash 3} - \frac{3}{2}x^{2}} \right)dx}}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= \left. {\frac{3}{7}x^{7 \slash 3} + \frac{3}{10}x^{5 \slash 3} - \frac{1}{2}x^{3}} \right|_{0}^{1}}} \\ {\phantom{\int_{R}{\int{\left( {x + y} \right)dA}}}{= \frac{3}{7} + \frac{3}{10} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{8}{35}}} \end{array}$$

image.alt: Details A line and a curve are graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes ranges from 0 to beyond 1. The line labeled y = x begins at origin, rises linearly upward to the right, passes through (1, 1) and extends further. The curve y = x^(1/3) begins at origin, rises upward steeply at first and then gradually to the right, concave down, intersects the line at (1, 1) and extends further. The region bounded by the curve and the line is shaded and labeled R.

$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = x + 2y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by the lines $$x = 1$$ , $$y = 0$$ , and $$y = x$$ .

$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2x + 4y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = 1$$ , $$x = 3$$ , $$y = 0$$ , and $$y = x + 1$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2 - y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = - 1$$ , $$x = 1 - y$$ , $$y = 0$$ , and $$y = 2$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = x + y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = 0$$ , $$x = \sqrt{y}$$ , and $$y = 4$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = 0$$ , $$x = \sqrt{4 - y^{2}}$$ , and $$y = 0$$ .

$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2xe^{y}$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by the lines $$x = 1$$ , $$y = 0$$ , and $$y = x$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2x$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = e^{2y}$$ , $$x = y$$ , $$y = 0$$ , and $$y = 1$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = ye^{x}$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}$$ and $$y = x$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = xe^{- y^{2}}$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = 0$$ , $$x = \sqrt{y}$$ , and $$y = 4$$ .

$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = y$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$y = \ln x$$ , $$x = e$$ , and $$y = 0$$ .
$$f\left( {x,y} \right) = ye^{x^{3}}$$ ; $$R$$ is bounded by $$x = \frac{y}{2}$$ , $$x = 1$$ , and $$y = 0$$ .

problem.paragraph: If $$h\left( {x,y} \right) = f(x)g(y)$$ , where $$f$$ is continuous on $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ and $$g$$ is continuous on $$\left\lbrack {c,d} \right\rbrack$$ , then $$\int_{R}{\int{h\left( {x,y} \right)dA = \left\lbrack {\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx}} \right\rbrack\left\lbrack {\int_{c}^{d}{g(y)dy}} \right\rbrack}}$$ , where $$R = \left\{ {\left. \left( {x,y} \right) \right|a \leq x \leq b;c \leq y \leq d} \right\}$$ .

If $$\int_{R_{1}}{\int{f\left( {x,y} \right)dA}}$$ exists, where $$R_{1} = \left\{ {\left. \left( {x,y} \right) \right|a \leq x \leq b;c \leq y \leq d} \right\}$$ , then $$\int_{R_{2}}{\int{f\left( {x,y} \right)dA}}$$ exists, where $$R_{2} = \left\{ {\left. \left( {x,y} \right) \right|c \leq x \leq d;a \leq y \leq b} \right\}$$ .
